amendment_type: Fixed-discharge inverse area/speed
teacher_review_note: For unchanged Q and mean normal speed, halving area doubles speed. This is source D with an unbranched steady incompressible/no-leak assumption.

amendment_type: Threefold widening
teacher_review_note: A₂=3A₁ leads to v₂=v₁/3 only for fixed Q; original C is valid.

amendment_type: Threefold speed implies one-third area
teacher_review_note: v₂=3v₁ leads A₂=A₁/3 with unchanged discharge; source A.

amendment_type: Diameter scales area quadratically
teacher_review_note: For a circular section A=πd²/4, halving d makes area 1/4, not 1/2; source D. Geometry is supporting continuity practice.

amendment_type: Diameter halved quadruples mean speed at fixed Q
teacher_review_note: A₂/A₁=(d₂/d₁)²=1/4, so v₂/v₁=4 under the expressly fixed flow rate; source D.

amendment_type: Area-speed product conserved
teacher_review_note: Area doubles and speed halves give unchanged Av. Source B is the only listed constant-discharge change.

amendment_type: Squeezed-hose speed rises only conditionally
teacher_review_note: The source says 'usually' and 'approximately': a smaller outlet area increases mean speed IF discharge stays approximately maintained. In real supplied hoses, pressure losses and pump/tap behavior can change Q, so do not teach the rise as unconditional. Original B remains best and B-37 is Summative/Understanding.

amendment_type: Correct source option B truncated during import
teacher_review_note: Genuine verbatim discrepancy: teacher-prepared PDF p.140 option B ends 'per second', but GitHub Q28 option B ends 'per'. Restore the missing word 'second' only after teacher authorization; original letter B and all other question texts/choices remain intact. Physically, gravity increases water-jet speed as the cross-sectional area narrows for nearly fixed Q, ignoring splashing, break-up and significant exchange.
source_option_B_text: Its speed increases while approximately the same water volume passes each level per
prepared_option_B_text: Its speed increases while approximately the same water volume passes each level per second

amendment_type: River effective area and average speed
teacher_review_note: Same discharge through two sections implies v=Q/A; greater effective area gives lower average speed, source D; tributaries/leaks between stations would change the mass balance.

amendment_type: Combined arterial area, not single-vessel area
teacher_review_note: If one aorta splits into thirty equal-size arteries and total branch area exceeds aortic area, individual branch mean speed can be lower when total discharge is conserved and split approximately across branches. The wording 'potentially' is crucial: no universal biological flow prediction follows without areas and branch distribution.

amendment_type: Compressible flow must retain density terms
teacher_review_note: For steady one-inlet/one-outlet gas flow with no leakage or accumulation, ṁ=ρAv stays constant while density can change; thus ρ₁A₁v₁=ρ₂A₂v₂ is the source best option D. Unsteady mass storage, branches or sources require a fuller continuity balance.

amendment_type: Pipe leakage changes downstream discharge
teacher_review_note: In a pipe with a loss of fluid between sections, downstream Q may be smaller; source B uses 'may', and remaining flow can still be nonzero.

amendment_type: Continuity does not demand equal pressure
teacher_review_note: Source C is correct: continuity conserves mass, not static pressure. This conceptual distinction supports B-38 but item-level Application classification still needs review.

amendment_type: Viscosity not necessary for mass conservation
teacher_review_note: Source C: continuity also applies to viscous real fluids. Recognizing this is Understanding, while official B-38 Application involves justifying the conservation principle.

amendment_type: Area ratio for speed ratios
teacher_review_note: v₂/v₁=A₁/A₂ under unchanged Q and nonzero section areas; source D algebraically correct.

amendment_type: Equal cross-sections give equal average speeds
teacher_review_note: For unchanged Q, A₁=A₂>0 implies equal mean speed magnitudes, source B. Velocity directions need not be identical at a bent section.

amendment_type: Y-junction sums outgoing volumetric rates only under appropriate conditions
teacher_review_note: Source B is correct for a steady incompressible split with no leaks or mass storage: Q_in=Q_out1+Q_out2. For compressible fluid, mass rates ρQ must be summed. This applies conservation-of-mass B-38 rather than merely adding volumes.

amendment_type: Nonzero discharge requires nonzero mean speed
teacher_review_note: If finite A is strictly positive, Q=Av≠0 means v≠0; source D. This is a conceptual implication of continuity.

amendment_type: Area tripling plus speed doubling contradicts fixed unbranched flow
teacher_review_note: The given simultaneous changes make A₂v₂=6A₁v₁, an algebraically sixfold Q increase; these changes cannot both occur in a steady incompressible, unbranched, no-leak pipe at equal throughput. Source B explicitly recognizes the incompatibility; teacher should emphasize this isn't a physically permitted two-section state under default assumptions.

amendment_type: Tributary adds mass and discharge between stations
teacher_review_note: In a steady incompressible river, Q₂=Q₁+Q_tributary minus any withdrawals between stations, so A₁v₁=A₂v₂ alone is generally invalid. Original A correctly requires an additional incoming term; don't assume constant Q across the confluence.
